articleTitle: New partitioning technology permits FPGA prototypes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: In this paper, a new package partitioning tool from Innovative Synthesis Technologies is described that uses functional cone partitioning (ICCAD93) to find high size to I/O ratio partitions. Partitioning for performance is provided by containing whole critical paths within packages, made easy with functional cone partitioning. Hierarchy is respected, allowing for partitioning into heterogeneous devices. As an extension of the ASYL+ netlist synthesis and technology migration system, the tool partitions for multiple PLD, FPGA, and ASIC technologies for desired market price and performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast prototyping complex digital systems: a case study using Reed-Solomon codes
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: This paper has considered the prototyping of a (31, 9) RS codec using FPGAs. It has been shown that using FPGAs in this role allows for fast, flexible and cheap prototypes to be produced. Unfortunately due to the complexity of the design four FPGAs were required to implement the codec and this prohibited the use of FPGAs as the target architecture on which to embed the codecs. It has also been shown that these FPGAs did demonstrate a number of limitations as RS codec development tools, namely their levels of hardware, their preference for bit-serial architectures and the manner in which combinational logic was implemented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using Handel to accelerate systems development
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: The Handel compiler, based on an Occam subset, is intended to exploit the expressive power of contemporary software engineering technology to rapidly generate high confidence net-list descriptions. These, once placed and routed, make efficient use of the target hardware (currently Xilinx FPGAs). This process is illustrated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Logic simulation for rapid prototyping: necessary or inhibiting?
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: In the course of numerous projects where we utilised User Programmable Logic Devices (UPLD) as a very feasible solution for building hardware system prototypes, we were often forced to decide how much simulation effort is acceptable to stay within time. In this survey we will show by means of several examples that both reliable logic and system simulation are-although sometimes quite time consuming-indispensable prerequisites for fast and efficient prototyping. Especially when dealing with complex UPLDs regardless of specific families, the turn around time of the placement and routing procedure exceeds several hours even if executed on high performance workstations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: Rapid prototyping is an "enabling" technology, bringing true simultaneous engineering and time compression to many organisations. These technologies are generally considered to be the process by which a facsimile model or (in certain circumstances) a master pattern is manufactured by layering techniques, directly from CAD data. However, unless rapid prototyping technologies are considered in context, and as a part of a much larger discipline, then typically many organisations will. gain very little commercial advantage by simply producing quick "hi-tech" models.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: Fast prototyping is a very important process in the pre-manufacturing flow to both customer and the semiconductor supplier. The customer having defined the system is then eager to test the initial prototype of the system. This is fine for systems that can use standard components which are freely available and will not hold up a project. However, fast prototyping is very important if time to market to the customer is required, especially if custom digital and analogue is required. More and more engineers in Europe are using ASICs. This is important as the cost reduction is now coming from semiconductor integration rather than in the good old days when printed circuit board layout was the easy cost reduction path. Large companies are using ASICs. FPGAs (field programmable gate arrays) are an excellent way of building the digital part of the system. If the product is mostly digital with simple analog then everything is fine. However, if price is the issue then a mixed mode ASIC will win on volume every time. Further problems come when the customer requires a breadboard built with FPGAs but the analogue section is high performance. The final product may have a specification requiring RFI to be very low and the problem may be compounded by dimensional constraints. A microASIC is often required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A complete integrated framework for ASIC and FPGA design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Fast Prototyping of IC Designs
abstract: Compass ASIC Synthesizer recognises through an HDL description which operators and variables can be mapped onto an X-BLOX element and creates the specification for the Xilinx X-BLOX compiler. This new technique is based upon a powerful recognition mechanism in the HDL code and allows several operators to be implemented into a single element. For example an addition into a memory variable will be implemented into a single accumulator. Such a tool now gives, in most cases, far better results than using classical optimization tools and even specific FPGA optimization tools.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
